title: Contingent Contracts
description: When you disagree about the future, bet on it instead of arguing.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: If the two sides disagree about what will happen — will it sell, will it cost this much, will it launch on time — a contingent contract turns the disagreement into a wager. Each side's prediction is tested against reality.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: A bet exposes confidence. Someone who truly believes their forecast will accept terms that pay off if they are right, which filters out bluffing and settles disputes that argument cannot.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: A bonus that pays only if delivery happens by an agreed date.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: "If X happens, you get Y; if not, I do."
Terms that pay differently depending on a future outcome.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Identify the disagreement about the future, then design a term where each side profits if their prediction is right. Keep it simple and measurable.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Contingencies so complex no one can verify them.
Bets on things outside either side's control.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Only accept a contingency you can verify and that reflects a real difference of view.
Beware terms that are actually a disguised penalty.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Arguing about forecasts instead of betting on them.
Designing contracts too complicated to enforce.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Bets resolve disagreements about the future.
Confidence should be willing to be tested.
